title: Coprime generators in a regular local surface are unit or maximal-primary
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak n)$ be a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] of Krull dimension $2$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Let $g_1,\ldots,g_r\in A$ be a finite list such that every element of $A$ dividing every $g_i$ is a unit. Put $J=(g_1,\ldots,g_r)$. Then either $J=A$, or $\sqrt{J}=\mathfrak n$.

source.place: Tag 0C48, proof of lemma-reduced-quotient-regular-ring-dim-2: after writing the generators as a common gcd times coprime residual generators, the paragraph beginning 'Thus the gcd of g_1, ..., g_r is 1'.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-regular-local-ufd-boundary-factorization] with the empty parameter sublist ($r=0$ in that lemma). It says in particular that $A$ is a nonzero Noetherian integral domain and a UFD. The ideal $J$ is nonzero: if $J=0$, every $g_i=0$, so $0$ divides every $g_i$; the hypothesis would make $0$ a unit, contrary to $A\ne0$. This also excludes an empty list of generators. If $J=A$ we have the first alternative; assume henceforth that $J\ne A$.

In a local ring the elements outside $\mathfrak n$ are units. Thus any proper ideal, in particular $J$ and any prime $\mathfrak p$ containing $J$, is contained in $\mathfrak n$: an element outside $\mathfrak n$ in such an ideal would put $1$ in it. For any such prime, $\mathfrak p

If a prime $\mathfrak q$ satisfied $0\subsetneq\mathfrak q\subsetneq\mathfrak p$, then $0\subsetneq\mathfrak q\subsetneq\mathfrak p\subsetneq\mathfrak n$ would be a prime chain of length $3$, contradicting $\dim A=2$ by [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Here $0$ is prime because $A$ is a domain, and $\mathfrak n$ is prime because it is maximal. Consequently $\mathfrak p$ has height one: it is nonzero and no prime lies strictly between $0$ and $\mathfrak p$.

For the hypothetical nonmaximal prime $\mathfrak p$ in Step 2, apply the implication (i)$\Rightarrow$(ii) of [lem-trf-ufd-height-one]. Its hypotheses hold because Step 1 gives a Noetherian UFD domain. Hence $\mathfrak p=(a)$ for some $a\in A$. Since $J\subseteq\mathfrak p$, each $g_i$ is a multiple of $a$, so the divisor hypothesis makes $a$ a unit. This gives $\mathfrak p=A$, contradicting the properness of a prime ideal. Thus every prime containing $J$ is $\mathfrak n$.

We have $J\subseteq\mathfrak n$ by Step 2, so $\mathfrak n$ itself is a prime containing $J$; Step 3 shows it is the only one. The radical/intersection formula in [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq] therefore gives $\sqrt J=\bigcap_{\mathfrak p\supseteq J}\mathfrak p=\mathfrak n$. This is the second alternative, completing the dichotomy.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q15-eb4e3007a (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, the source and every cited node in full. Source: Stacks curves.tex lines 3816–3849, lemma-reduced-quotient-regular-ring-dim-2; tags/tags line 15218 confirms it is Tag 0C48. The item states exactly the first paragraph of that proof: a regular local ring of dimension 2, generators whose only common divisors are units, and the conclusion J=A or sqrt J = n. It is not weakened and is unchanged from the base. Step 1 uses only the statement of lem-trf-regular-local-ufd-boundary-factorization with the empty sublist (r=0 is allowed); that statement gives a Noetherian UFD domain. The step also shows J is nonzero: an empty or all-zero list would make 0 a common divisor, hence a unit, which is impossible. Step 2 is genuinely elementary: a nonmaximal prime above J with a nonzero prime strictly below it would give a chain 0<q<p<n of length 3, contradicting the definition of dimension in def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring; so the prime has height one in exactly the sense used by lem-trf-ufd-height-one. Step 3 applies the (i)=>(ii) direction of lem-trf-ufd-height-one (a Mathlib leaf, Stacks 0AFT); its Noetherian-domain hypotheses come from Step 1. The prime is then principal, its generator is a unit, and that is a contradiction. Step 4 applies lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq (a Mathlib leaf, Stacks 00E0(7)) to V(J)={n} to get sqrt J = n. proof_deps equals the union of the steps' uses. Route: the two statement citations are in the unit sk-i-curve-zero; the off-unit citations are two definition nodes and one Mathlib leaf. No tool_uses are needed and none were accepted; there is no SGA citation. The item's dependency closure (135 nodes) does not contain the item, so there is no cycle. The only citer, lem-trf-regular-surface-depth-one-principal, uses both alternatives consistently with the statement. A whole-DAG search for 0C48 and its label, 'height one prime', gcd and 'common divisor' found no duplicate or generalization. There are no new nodes. Small cases in k[[x,y]]: (x,y) and (x^2,y^2) have radical n, (x,1+y) is A, (x^2,xy) and a single nonunit break the hypothesis, and in dimension 3 the ideal (x,y) shows the dimension-2 hypothesis is needed. lean.statement: theorem coprimeGeneratorsMprimaryOrUnit (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsRegularLocalRing A] (hdim : ringKrullDim A = (2 : WithBot ℕ∞)) (r : ℕ) (g : Fin r → A) (hdiv : ∀ d : A, (∀ i : Fin r, d ∣ g i) → IsUnit d) : Ideal.span (Set.range g) = ⊤ ∨ (Ideal.span (Set.range g)).radical = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A
